judge.rationale: The implementation is a textbook realization of the Zero-Trust Audit Principle ZT-2. It computes the access decision first, then unconditionally appends a complete log record containing role, permission, and allowed before returning — there is no code path that can bypass the log write. The logic is flat (no nesting beyond a single function body), explicit (deny-by-default via an empty-set fallback), and locally auditable at a glance. Type annotations are precise, the docstring accurately describes the contract, and the variable names are self-documenting. There is no architectural slop: no classes, no decorators, no hidden state, no unnecessary abstraction.

- Every access attempt must be logged before returning, whether allowed or denied.
- No short-circuit return may bypass the log write.
- Log records must include role, permission, and allowed.
